# Wise Women Use AI

> Practical AI education and consulting for women in business, founded by
> Kelly Hartley, an AI consultant and educator based in Melbourne, Australia.
> Warm, jargon-free teaching that works around real life, not hustle culture.

Kelly Hartley is a British-Australian business owner who runs her own
businesses on AI (primarily Claude) and teaches women in midlife to do the
same. WWUAI is not another ChatGPT course. It teaches Claude specifically,
with a focus on simple systems women can actually stick to. Kelly also works
one-to-one as an AI consultant, based in Melbourne and working online with
women across Australia.

Everything runs on the same three steps. The free monthly workshop is the
first win, where you build the smallest real piece yourself and keep it. The
membership is the complete system, built over six guided steps a month with a
room of women doing the same. The Advantage Pack is that system already built
and installed, so you duplicate it and it is running.

## Work with Kelly
- [AI Consulting, Melbourne and online](https://www.wisewomenuseai.com/work): One-to-one AI setup and strategy sessions, and a four-week done-with-you systems build
- [About Kelly Hartley](https://www.wisewomenuseai.com/about): Who Kelly is and why she built WWUAI

## Community and membership
- [Skool Community](https://www.wisewomenuseai.com/community): Free to join. The Unfair Advantage is the paid membership inside ($69 USD/month, billed by Skool) with the full library of tools, prompts and workflows
- [Free monthly workshop](https://www.wisewomenuseai.com/workshop): Live online workshop, one hour, free. Kelly shows the real tools and walks people through setting them up, so attendees leave having built the first piece themselves

## Products
- [The Notion Advantage Pack](https://www.wisewomenuseai.com/notion-advantage): A ready-built Notion business system, installed rather than assembled
- [The Content Advantage Pack](https://www.wisewomenuseai.com/content-advantage): A ready-built content system: a 13-week calendar, a hook bank, a prompt library that keeps your voice, and a Notion Content Command Centre

## Free guides and starters
- [Claude, Clearly](https://www.wisewomenuseai.com/guide): Free guide to getting started with Claude
- [Switch to Claude](https://www.wisewomenuseai.com/switch): Free guide for ChatGPT users moving to Claude
- [Claude Starter Kit](https://www.wisewomenuseai.com/starter): Free starter resources for brand-new Claude users
- [The Sunday Reset](https://www.wisewomenuseai.com/calm): Four prompts that turn a full head into a sorted week
- [Where does your week actually go?](https://www.wisewomenuseai.com/hours): A one minute count of the jobs that quietly eat a small business owner's week
- [Seven tells that make writing sound like AI](https://www.wisewomenuseai.com/slop): The list, in plain English, with the prompt that catches them
- [Carousel Maker](https://www.wisewomenuseai.com/carousel-maker): A free Claude Code skill file that turns brand photos into Instagram carousels

## Writing
- [Blog](https://www.wisewomenuseai.com/blog): Practical AI for women in business
- [AI for Solopreneurs in Australia](https://www.wisewomenuseai.com/posts/ai-for-solopreneurs-australia): What actually works in 2026

## Transparency
- [How I use AI](https://www.wisewomenuseai.com/ai-disclosure): Kelly's open disclosure of exactly where AI does the work in this business, what stays hers, and what she will not use it for
- [Privacy](https://www.wisewomenuseai.com/privacy): What is collected, where it is kept, and how to have it removed. No tracking pixels, no analytics, no advertising cookies on this site

  Note for whoever maintains this: no AI system is known to read /llms.txt.
  Google's John Mueller said so publicly in June 2025 ("no AI system currently
  uses llms.txt"), Gary Illyes confirmed Google has no plans to support it, and
  Google's own AI-features documentation says you do not need to create AI text
  files to appear in its AI features. It was a proposal, not an agreed standard,
  and adoption is entirely on the publishing side.

  It is kept because it is cheap, harmless, and readable by a human. Do not
  expand it, and do not treat it as an AEO lever. What actually decides whether
  this site is quoted in an AI answer: ordinary search ranking, being
  crawlable (see robots.txt), and clear on-page answers in visible text.
  Checked 12 August 2026.
